payload.prompt: A software team is matching model families to work: code reasoning, multilingual business reports, and a planning-heavy agent. Which choices are well supported?

options.text: GPT-5.x for multi-step reasoning and planning.
options.rationale: GPT-5.x is optimized for multi-step reasoning, structured logic, planning, and agentic workflows. That directly fits planning-heavy work.

options.text: Claude Opus 4.5 for complex code reasoning.
options.rationale: Claude Opus 4.5 supports complex code reasoning and sophisticated agents. It also supports long specifications and multi-file diffs.

options.text: Mistral Large 3 for multilingual drafting.
options.rationale: Mistral Large 3 supports multilingual drafting and structured business report generation. It is a general model with cost and latency trade-offs.

options.text: GPT-5.x for the lowest-latency high-volume chat by default.
options.error_type: confuses GPT-5.x reasoning strengths with GPT-4.1 low-latency chat
options.rationale: GPT-5.x is best aligned with reasoning-heavy planning and agentic workflows. GPT-4.1 is the model for speed, efficiency, and low-latency inference.
options.better_fit: Use GPT-4.1 for real-time chat, customer support, and fast interactive applications at scale.

feedback.intrinsic: The team may choose a reasoning-heavy family for a workload that mainly needs quick responses.
feedback.instructional: Separate reasoning depth from response speed; the named low-latency option is GPT-4.1.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The supported matches use each family for its strengths.

payload.prompt: A support lead must launch a high-volume customer chat app soon. A teammate suggests GPT-5.x because it is reasoning-heavy. Which points should guide the choice?

options.text: GPT-5 requires registration, so availability is restricted.
options.rationale: Restricted availability matters when the support lead needs to launch soon. GPT-5.x is not broadly available to all Foundry users.

options.text: GPT-4.1 is available to all Foundry users.
options.rationale: GPT-4.1 is available to all Foundry users. That matters for a team that needs an accessible option for a near-term launch.

options.text: GPT-4.1 is optimized for speed and low latency.
options.rationale: GPT-4.1 is optimized for speed, efficiency, and low-latency inference. Those strengths fit high-volume customer support chat.

options.text: GPT-4.1 is mainly for long-context reasoning trade-offs.
options.error_type: confuses GPT-4.1 with reasoning-heavy model families
options.rationale: GPT-4.1 fits fast interactive applications that respond quickly and at scale. Long-context reasoning and adjustable thinking trade-offs are GPT-5.x strengths.
options.better_fit: Use GPT-5.x when multi-step reasoning, planning, and long-context understanding are the main needs.

feedback.intrinsic: The support lead may overlook the fast chat option and choose for the wrong strength.
feedback.instructional: For high-volume support, prioritize the model with availability, speed, and low latency.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The launch need points toward broad availability and low latency, not just reasoning depth.
